title: Lakemont Support Grid — Enterprise Onboarding Plan (2025)
author: Priya Nair
content:
## Overview
Lakemont Support Grid (HG-47821, lakemontgrid.com) is an enterprise financial services customer onboarding for contact-center automation. The initial deployment targets NA support teams with an expansion plan for EU and APAC. This page is the canonical onboarding reference for Customer Success + Solutions Engineering.

**Account snapshot (latest):**
- Account tier: Enterprise
- Commercial stage: Contracting / final procurement steps (SOW redlines in progress)
- Primary owner (GTM): Avery Chen
- Assigned SE: Diego Morales
- Assigned CSM: Priya Nair

## Products and use cases
**Interested products:** Dedicated, Private, Optimize

**Primary use cases (2025 rollout):**
- Real-time agent assist (suggested replies, next-best actions)
- Post-call / post-chat ticket summarization
- Tool calling (create/update tickets; annotate CRM records)
- Quality monitoring (QA sampling + rubric scoring)
- IVR handoff support (context packaging for handoff)

## Current environment and integration scope
**Systems in scope:**
- Zendesk (NA pilot + initial production)
- In-house CRM (tool-calling writebacks; limited initial fields)

**Integration notes:**
- Tool calling is required for ticket creation and CRM writes.
- Masking/redaction must be applied before any non-residency-safe routing.

## Workload, performance targets, and success metrics
### Traffic assumptions
- Baseline: ~450 concurrent agent sessions
- Peak: up to ~1,400 concurrent sessions during end-of-month + incident events
- Spike behavior: capacity must degrade gracefully; no hard failures for agent UX paths

### Latency / throughput targets
- Agent-assist suggestion generation: p95 <= 300–350ms (UX-critical)
- Throughput target during spikes: ~2,000 requests/sec aggregate (mix of assist + tool calls)

### Quality / business outcomes
- Summarization accuracy target: >= 88% on Lakemont internal QA rubric (updated from earlier 85% target)
- Handle-time reduction target: 15–20%
- Adoption guardrail: if p95 latency or correctness regressions occur, agents may disable assist; performance is non-negotiable.

## Deployment model and security/compliance requirements
### Deployment
- Primary: VPC-based Private deployment
- On-prem: No longer required for initial NA/EU rollout; only a potential future requirement for narrowly scoped PCI-adjacent subsystems (pending final PCI scoping).

### Data residency
- EU transcripts and derived artifacts must remain in-region.
- Proposed regions:
  - NA: us-east-1
  - EU: eu-central-1 (Frankfurt)
- Residency enforcement must apply to:
  - Raw transcripts
  - Intermediate prompts/contexts
  - Stored summaries/embeddings (if enabled)
  - Audit logs containing customer content

### Security controls (confirmed requirements)
- SSO: SAML SSO mandatory
- Key management: customer-managed KMS integration (AWS KMS CMK preferred)
- Audit logging: required; retention 7+ years
- Certifications/evidence: ISO 27001 evidence required; SOC 2 deep dive completed (see timeline)

## Dedicated capacity plan (updated)
Earlier sizing guidance (2 GPU nodes + hosted burst) was revised after EU throughput/latency discussions.

**Current recommendation (for NA + EU readiness):**
- NA Dedicated pool: 2 GPU nodes (baseline) with headroom for typical spikes
- EU Dedicated pool: 3 GPU nodes to meet p95 latency targets under peak concurrency assumptions
- Burst strategy: allowed only under residency-safe routing policy. EU traffic must not route out-of-region. NA traffic may burst to hosted only if masking rules are met.

**Open sizing deliverable:** Provide explicit p95 latency expectations per region under 4 setups (NA-only, EU-only, dual-region active/active, dual-region active/passive) and the overflow behavior.

## Fallback and routing policy (required for sign-off)
**Principles:**
1) EU traffic never leaves EU region.
2) When Dedicated capacity is exceeded, overflow is permitted only to a residency-safe target.
3) Any overflow to shared/hosted requires masking and content minimization.

**Action item:** Finalize the written policy and share with Lakemont security + procurement (appendix to SOW).

## Onboarding plan and milestones
### Phase 1 — NA pilot (extended)
- Duration: 8-week pilot (updated from initial 6-week plan)
- Users: 100 NA agents
- Scope: agent assist + ticket summarization + limited tool calling into Zendesk
- Success criteria:
  - p95 <= 350ms for assist
  - Suggestion acceptance lift >= 10%
  - No PII leakage events

### Phase 2 — EU pilot
- Users: 50 EU agents
- Scope: validate data residency, audit logging, and EU Dedicated sizing
- Deliverable: security sign-off for EU go-live

### Phase 3 — Production rollout
- Staged rollout by queue/team with weekly quality and latency reviews
- Expand tool-calling writebacks (CRM fields) after stability gates

## Timeline (key events)
- 2024-09-18: Initial inbound; account created
- 2024-11-04: Discovery call; “latency is non-negotiable” emphasized by Head of Support
- 2024-12-03: Infra + security checklist review (Fireflies ff-20241203-9012)
- 2025-01-08: POC kickoff (Fireflies ff-20250108-4821); NA pilot agreed
- 2025-01-23: Initial infra sizing recommendation from SE; proposal v2 shared
- 2025-02-05: Data residency appendix + PCI scoping questions raised (internal tracking SEC-1121)
- 2025-02-25: SOC 2 / security deep dive completed; follow-ups documented in security Q&A
- 2025-03-05: EU throughput SLA discussion; Dedicated pool recommendation updated for EU

## Blockers / risks (current)
- Legal review: SOW redlines + data residency appendix finalization
- Regional data residency: confirm enforcement approach for artifacts (summaries/embeddings)
- PCI scope questions: determine whether any flows must be isolated beyond Private VPC deployment
- Latency/SLA clarification: commit language for p95 expectations and measurement methodology

## Operational readiness (CS + SE checklist)
**Before production go-live:**
1) Confirm identity integration (SAML) and least-privilege roles
2) Confirm KMS integration and key rotation responsibilities
3) Enable audit logging; validate retention and access controls
4) Define performance dashboards (p95 latency, error rates, throughput, token utilization)
5) Establish incident and escalation paths (Lakemont + Redwood)
6) Run load test in NA and EU with agreed traffic model
7) Validate data residency controls with security team sign-off
